description.narrative: Mongolian Railway JSC (MTZ or the Company) is a wholly state-owned rail company established in 2008 to develop, own, and operate state-funded rail assets in Mongolia. It is one of the two public rail carriers in the country and a pivotal player in the national railway sector. MTZ operates several freight rail lines with a total length of over 650 km. IFC is considering financing the construction of the Bagakhangai-Khushig Valley branch railway (the Project), which is a greenfield 87.7 km single-track railway branching off from the Bagakhangai station on the Trans-Mongolia Railway and terminating at Khushig Valley. The Project is designed to divert rail freight from central Ulaanbaatar, with subsequent phases supporting relocation of city-based logistics to a new multimodal hub at Khushig Valley and completion of a full rail bypass. The Project is expected to reduce urban congestion, improve urban air quality, and enhance logistics efficiency and competitiveness, thus improving the overall liveability of the capital city.

The Project contributes to Ulaanbaatars urban transformation by diverting rail freight traffic not destined for Ulaanbaatar away from the urban core, thus reducing congestion and improving urban mobility with environmental co-benefits. Its also expected to create jobs for Mongolians. At the market level, the Project is expected to increase competitiveness by supporting the development of a modern multimodal logistics hub on the citys outskirts that will consolidate fragmented logistics operations, thereby improving efficiency and connectivity in Mongolia.
